title: The hint renderer turns a nested \sqrt in \frac, and subscripts, into maths
body:
## Summary
maths() rewrote \frac before \sqrt and had no subscript rule, so two hints reached the TV as raw LaTeX.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:462-465 (base): the \frac pattern allows no brace in its arguments, so a \sqrt inside it (the quadratic formula) stayed raw; "$y_2$" showed "y_2". Fixed: inner \sqrt first, then \frac; _d to subscript digits.

## Flow
- open the hint for 2x^2-5x-3=0, Still stuck
- before: "x = \frac{-b ± √(b² - 4ac)}{2a}"
- after: "x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))⁄(2a)"

## Expected impact
The prototype shows the real hints readably. Other 86 lines render byte-identically; Spanish blanks keep their underscores.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - hints render as maths
Before: 2 of 88 hint lines still show LaTeX
After: 0 of 88
Method: probe - the page's own maths() over every hint line in data.json; no gate covers prototype/
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A task name typed on the phone is escaped before it reaches the task lists
body:
## Summary
The phone's "Add an assignment" text went raw into innerHTML in the TV task row and the phone list.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:386 and :618 (base) interpolated t.name into innerHTML; prototype/linga-conversations.html:37 escapes every string through esc(). A name with "<" lost text or ran script. Fixed: esc() on t.name and t.sub.

## Flow
- phone: Add an assignment "Read <Macbeth> act 2"
- before: the TV row shows "Read  act 2"; an onerror tag runs
- after: the text as typed

## Expected impact
Typed names show as typed; the page cannot be scripted from the input. Could break: nothing seen; seeded tasks render as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - typed text renders as text
Before: 6 of 6 list renders carry the typed name as raw markup
After: 0 of 6
Method: probe - the page's script under a DOM stub with the real data.json; no gate covers prototype/
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A lesson opened again starts playing instead of inheriting the last pause
body:
## Summary
S.paused outlived the lesson screen, so a reopened lesson sat frozen and labelled paused.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:493 (base) openLesson reset the clock to the lesson mark but not S.paused; the tick (:494) does nothing while paused. Fixed: openLesson clears the pause.

## Flow
- lesson: Space (pause), Backspace
- hint: Show me the lesson
- before: "0:01 / 7:25 · paused", no tick; after: playing

## Expected impact
The reopened lesson plays from its mark, as a fresh open does.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a fresh open plays
Before: reopened lessons that start paused: 1 of 1
After: 0 of 1
Method: probe - DOM-stub harness drives the keydown handler
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
prototype/src/index.html:493 (base) lessonT = L.t; renderLesson(); show("lesson");  // S.paused untouched
prototype/src/index.html:494 setInterval(() => { if (S.screen !== "lesson" || S.paused) return; ... })

title: build.py's script-tag guard ignores case, as the HTML parser does
body:
## Summary
build.py escaped only the lower-case "</script" when inlining data.json into a script block.

## Description
prototype/build.py:34 (base) raw.replace("</script", "<\\/script"); the HTML tokenizer ends a script block on the tag in any case. Fixed: re.sub with re.I, keeping the original case.

## Flow
- a hint containing "</SCRIPT>" in data.json
- before: the page script ends early, the rest of the data prints as text
- after: escaped

## Expected impact
The guard does what its comment says. Today's data has none, so the output is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the inlining guard covers every spelling
Before: 1 of 3 closing-tag spellings neutralised
After: 3 of 3; guard(data) == data both sides
Method: probe - the guard read from the file, three spellings
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Drop PHOTO_W, a page-width helper nothing calls
body:
## Summary
prototype/src/index.html defined PHOTO_W and nothing called it.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:395 (base) const PHOTO_W = () => S.pages[S.pageIx].w; renderPage reads p.w itself. grep -rn PHOTO_W prototype/: the definition only. Removed.

## Flow
- grep PHOTO_W -> 1 hit, the definition
- remove it; the page script still runs under the probe harness

## Expected impact
One fewer name to read. Nothing can break: no consumer.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - dead code removed
Before: 1 definition, 0 consumers
After: 0, 0
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep; page script run under the harness after
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A D-pad press no longer rewrites the page strip's inline photos
body:
## Summary
renderPage rebuilt the thumbnail strip, each thumb an inline data: photo, on every D-pad press.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:419-420 (base) set strip.innerHTML with every page's data URI on each renderPage, which runs per press. Fixed: rebuild when the set of pages changes; a press flips data-current.

## Flow
- three pages captured, Up/Down on the page
- before: 476 KB of markup re-parsed per press
- after: 0; the strip still grows when a page is added

## Expected impact
D-pad presses on the page stop re-parsing the photos. Could break: the current-thumb outline (same attribute, same CSS).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - work per input event
Before: 10 rewrites, 476 KB markup per press (10 presses, 3 pages)
After: 0 rewrites, 0 KB
Method: probe - DOM-stub harness counts strip innerHTML writes
Result: better
Gate: none

title: build.py names a missing maths page and writes nothing, not a bare StopIteration
body:
## Summary
build.py wrote study-desk.html, then a bare next() for the math page raised StopIteration, leaving half a build.

## Description
prototype/build.py:37 (base) next(p for p in ... if p["id"] == "math") after the first write(); write() itself stops the build with a named reason for a placeholder (build.py:22-24), the lookup did not. Fixed: the lookup runs before any write and exits with its reason.

## Flow
- data.json without the math page
- before: StopIteration traceback, study-desk.html written
- after: "build: data.json has no page with id \"math\" and an img", nothing written

## Expected impact
A broken data.json says what is wrong and leaves no stale pair.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a build failure names its cause
Before: exit 1, StopIteration, 1 of 2 outputs written
After: exit 1, named reason, 0 of 2
Method: probe - build run on a temp copy with the page removed
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
prototype/build.py:37 (base) math = next(p for p in json.loads(raw)["pages"] if p["id"] == "math")
probe before: StopIteration; study-desk.html present in the temp dir

title: Spanish and essay hints disable the lesson button and never say why
body:
## Summary
The "No lesson in tonight's library" line shows only for maths, so 10 hint screens show a dead button with no reason.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:457 sets noneBox only when h.subject === "math" && !pick; Spanish and essay have no picks in data.json, so btnLesson is disabled with nothing on screen. Proposed: show the line whenever there is no pick. Built and reverted: on a Spanish hint the line sits below the rule card and may collide with the absolutely-placed actions row (estimated ~900 px of 906 px), which no probe here can see.

## Flow
- Spanish page, item 1, Enter
- hint + rule card; "Show me the lesson" off, no reason
- proposal: the none line for any subject, checked against the actions row

## Expected impact
A learner sees why the button is off. Could break: the hint layout on long Spanish hints.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an off button says why
Before: 10 of 14 hint screens with the lesson button off show no reason
After: 0 of 14 (probe on the reverted build)
Method: probe - the count is measured; the layout overlap needs a capture
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
prototype/src/index.html:457 $("btnLesson").disabled = !pick; $("noneBox").style.display = (h.subject === "math" && !pick) ? "block" : "none";
probe: spanish 1-6, essay 1-4 "lesson button off, no reason shown"
instrument: a Playwright capture of the 10 Spanish/essay hint screens from the built study-desk.html (fonts blocked), asserting the none line's bottom is above .actions' top; seed red with a long hint

title: Three of four prototype pages render in quirks mode: no doctype, charset or lang
body:
## Summary
index.html, on-air.src.html and variants.html start at <title>; only linga-conversations.html has <!doctype html>, <meta charset> and lang.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:1, prototype/identity/on-air.src.html:1 and prototype/identity/variants.html:1 begin with <title>, so the browser renders them in quirks mode and guesses the encoding of their non-ASCII text (—, ², «»); prototype/linga-conversations.html:1-4 declares all three. The On Air page is the design reference for every TV screen, and the Next.js desk renders in standards mode, so the reference is drawn under different layout rules from the product. Proposed: the same three lines on each source page.

## Flow
- open study-desk.html -> document.compatMode === "BackCompat"
- proposal: <!doctype html><html lang="en"><meta charset="utf-8"> on the three sources
- capture each stage before and after

## Expected impact
The references render as the product does. Could break: any layout that leaned on quirks (line boxes, percentage heights), which only a pixel diff can show.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - references render in the product's mode
Before: pages without doctype/charset/lang: 3 of 4
After: predicted 0 of 4
Method: simulation - the count is grep-able; the layout effect of leaving quirks mode needs a browser capture this run cannot take
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
head -1: prototype/src/index.html "<title>Study Desk</title>"; prototype/identity/on-air.src.html "<title>Study Desk On Air</title>"; prototype/identity/variants.html "<title>Study Desk Identity</title>"
prototype/linga-conversations.html:1-4 <!doctype html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8">
instrument: Playwright: compatMode of each built page (BackCompat -> CSS1Compat) plus a pixel diff of every On Air and variant stage before/after, fonts blocked

title: Read-aloud speaks hints with their LaTeX left in
body:
## Summary
say() strips only $, \frac, \sqrt and *, so the speech of six hints carries "b^2", "y_2" and braces that the screen's maths() renders.

## Description
prototype/src/index.html:348 say() keeps its own stripper; maths() (:462) is the screen's. Six hint lines (hint1/hint2 .hint) hold LaTeX: e.g. "$b^2 - 4ac$" is spoken as "b^2 - 4ac". Two implementations of one rule, only the screen's maintained. Proposed: speak a speech form built from maths()'s output ("b squared", "y 2").

## Flow
- Read hints aloud on; open the quadratic hint
- speech: "b caret 2" (engine-dependent)
- proposal: one LaTeX-to-words pass for speech

## Expected impact
The read-aloud hint matches the screen. Could break: how a given TTS voice reads ² or ⁄.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - spoken hints read as maths
Before: spoken hints carrying LaTeX: 6 of 44
After: predicted 0 of 44
Method: simulation - the strings are counted; what a speech engine says needs a capture of SpeechSynthesisUtterance text and a listen
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
prototype/src/index.html:348 new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(t.replace(/\$|\\frac|\\sqrt|\*/g, ""))
6 hint strings with LaTeX: "$b^2 - 4ac$", "$x$", "$y$" x2, "x^2", "$y_2$ ... $x_1$"
instrument: harness capturing the utterance text for all 44 hints (count LaTeX tokens) plus one listen in Chrome by the operator
